QF.id: VIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_60

question.text: Stock ABC has a spot price of Rs. 1,500. It is expected to pay a dividend of Rs. 30 in 40 days. The risk-free rate is 8% and the futures expire in 90 days. Using the discrete dividend model, what is the fair futures price? (Hint: PV of dividend = 30/(1+0.08)^(40/365))

explanation.text: The Logic: Cost-of-carry pricing with a known discrete dividend uses the general form F = (S - PV(D)) x (1+r)^(T/365), where the dividend is first discounted back to today and then the dividend-adjusted spot is compounded forward to expiry. Applying this with S = 1,500, D = 30 at day 40, r = 8% and T = 90 days gives a futures price in the neighbourhood of Rs. 1,498-1,500 (the precise figure depends on rounding conventions and compounding choice), which is what the keyed answer captures. The Trap: Rs. 1,530 ignores the dividend entirely. Rs. 1,528.65 subtracts the dividend without first discounting it to present value. Rs. 1,470 subtracts the dividend but forgets to apply cost of carry forward to expiry. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (43-45) support cost-of-carry pricing and the adjustment of the spot for inflows/dividend yield, but the explicit discrete-dividend present-value form PV(D) = D/(1+r)^(days/365) was not located in those pages, and the exact keyed numeric (Rs. 1,499.44) differs by a small rounding margin from a literal application of the formula (which gives roughly Rs. 1,498.42). The framing above is general futures-pricing theory rather than a direct workbook citation.
